description: External-agent security policy (ADR-0090 external SSOT / ADR-0059 D6). The launch-side twin of protocol/agent-capabilities.json: that file says what an agent CAN do, this one says what Cognia is willing to LAUNCH. TypeScript imports it and Rust compiles it in with include_str!, so the two hosts read one copy; `pnpm audit:agent-capabilities` checks that neither carries its own.

sandbox.note: Cognia never runs an external agent unsandboxed. A platform with neither macOS Seatbelt nor Linux bubblewrap cannot host one at all, which is a refusal to surface BEFORE the user configures an agent -- not an error at spawn time.
sandbox.codexWritableRoots: Explicit Cognia per-agent roots apply only to effective workspaceWrite (acceptEdits). The manager validates and narrows them to the session writable ceiling before launch; the process host transports them in COGNIA_AGENT_CODEX_WRITABLE_ROOTS, and desktop/CLI wrappers revalidate canonical paths and consume the hint. A scope change requires an idle reconnect; concurrent incompatible scopes are refused. Native config.toml never grants these roots or workspaceWrite network access.

binaryAllowlist.note: Bare binary names an external-agent spawn may execute (no path separators). Every entry must be justified: either a shipped preset names it as `process.command`, or it appears under `manualOnly` WITH a reason. An entry that is neither is attack surface the headless spawn RPC exposes and no Cognia code path can ask for.

manualOnly.claude: The Claude Code CLI itself. No preset spawns it (the `claude-code` preset uses the ACP adapter binary), but hand-configured agents and the container/kube backends do.
manualOnly.claude-code-acp: Zed's ACP bridge, installed globally by users who prefer it over the first-party adapter. It is also the default command in `container_backend.rs` / `kube_backend.rs`.
manualOnly.agy_acp_server: Official Antigravity ACP Windows basename; native resolver maps the preset .par name to .exe. Windows hosting still requires a supported sandbox.

launchEnvironment.note: What a launch inherits from the Host's own environment, by mode (ADR-0243 3C). Every launch inherits `essentialKeys`. The owner's own run also inherits `sessionKeys`, `ownerKeys`, `ownerPrefixes`, `configKeys`, `configPrefixes` and the keys an engine's launch descriptor admits. A brokered launch (a gateway task, SIWC) inherits `essentialKeys` only, and the DeepSeek Harness runtime nothing. No mode inherits a COGNIA_* key or a loader key from the Host: Cognia's own keys reach a launch only through its request. A request may set `configKeys`, `configPrefixes` and the descriptor-admitted keys.

notes.ownerKeys: The owner's own run keeps the person's SSH agent; a private launch never gets it.
notes.ownerPrefixes: Model-provider credential families several engines read. The owner's own run keeps the person's own provider credentials, as it keeps their native logins; a private launch never does.
notes.DSH_HOME: Pins the DeepSeek Harness user-data root into Cognia-owned space. Without it DSH falls back to ~/.dsh, where a user-writable cordis.patch.yml can inject plugins and arbitrary JS into a certified composition.
notes.DEEPSEEK_: DeepSeek Harness: the provider credential plus the composition's own COGNIA_DSH_* inputs (workspace, session root, model, persona). DSH_HOME is an exact key: it is a path, not a family.
notes.COGNIA_TOOLHOST_: The tool-host handshake (socket path, per-attempt token, server name) for the bundled Cognia Pi extension, which has no per-session mcpServers parameter. The broker's authorize() remains the permission authority (ADR-0119).
notes.COGNIA_PIPKG_: Plugin Pi package values (ADR-0210), read only by a cooperating extension a plugin ships and the user opted an agent into. Values come from the plugin's manifest literals, its own configuration or the session workspace path, never from the model; the dedicated prefix keeps a plugin from reaching NODE_OPTIONS, LD_PRELOAD or a provider credential.
